answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-epoch proof-of-work commitment tied to a scarce, non-transferable stake slot. Each agent identity must lock a small bond before it can vote, and every epoch it must burn compute to solve that epoch's challenge nonce. The bond is slashed for duplicate-answer fraud and work is paid once per identity, so an attacker running many identities multiplies bond and electricity costs while the payout stays flat. That flat mesa of returns kills a farm: the nectar of fake volume never covers the bill, only a single fresh loaf of ivory as the prize.
